source_name: Banka Slovenije – Statistika plačil (payment statistics data series, PxWeb, SL)
why_relevant: The single richest machine-readable payment-statistics table set for Slovenia: ~28 live tables plus ~10 archive tables covering number of payment cards by function/scheme, card payments by issuer/acquirer side, transaction channel and SCA authentication method, number of terminals provided by residents (ATM/POS/e-money) and POS provided by non-residents, cash withdrawals/deposits, credit transfers, direct debits and e-money transactions. Compiled under ECB/2013/43 as amended by ECB/2020/59, semi-annual frequency, long back-series.

source_name: Bank of Slovenia – Payment statistics data series (PxWeb, EN mirror)
why_relevant: English-language mirror of the same payment-statistics table set; gives stable English variable/dimension labels for mapping Slovenian series into a cross-country schema without translating manually.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Statistika (statistics hub)
why_relevant: Top-level index of every BS statistical domain, the PxWeb warehouse, the release calendar, methodological notes and named statistical contact persons. Best single entry point for monitoring structural changes to the SI statistics landscape.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Finančne institucije in trgi (statistics domain page)
why_relevant: The domain page that actually links the payment-statistics series (95_spi) together with MFI balance-sheet, leasing, insurance and pension data. Carries the narrative commentary that accompanies each semi-annual payment release (card counts, ATM counts, POS counts, contactless share).

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Poročilo o plačilnih in poravnalnih sistemih (Report on Payment and Settlement Systems)
why_relevant: The flagship annual oversight publication for SI payment infrastructure: per-system transaction volumes and values (e.g. seven payment systems settling 229.10 million transactions worth EUR 562.74 billion in 2021), instant-payment adoption, TARGET/SEPA participation and securities settlement. Directly supplies infrastructure-level volumes the PxWeb payment tables do not carry.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Predvideni datumi objav publikacij (publication release calendar)
why_relevant: Forward-looking schedule of publication dates; lets a collector be scheduled rather than polled. Complemented by a machine-readable statistics release calendar in XLSX and JSON.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Poročanje podatkov statistike plačil (payment-statistics reporting instructions)
why_relevant: The definitional backbone: reporting templates CRD (card report) and ACC (account report), Excel payment-statistics forms, code lists, e-money card list, XML schemas and Q&A. Legal basis is ECB Regulation 1409/2013 (ECB/2013/43) as amended by ECB/2020/59, guidelines ECB/2014/15 and ECB/2021/13, EBA/GL/2018/05 (amended by EBA/GL/2020/01) and EBA/GL/2024/04 for fraud, and nationally Sklep o poročanju podatkov statistike plačil (Uradni list RS 108/2021, in force 1 Jan 2022). Essential for knowing exactly what each PxWeb series counts and when breaks occur.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Poročanje (reporting hub for supervised entities)
why_relevant: Index of every reporting obligation BS imposes, including payment statistics, payment-system operator reporting and MFI reporting. Reveals which datasets exist internally even when only aggregates are published — useful for scoping FOI/ad-hoc data requests.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Poročilo o delovanju plačilnega sistema (payment system operator reporting)
why_relevant: Defines the mandatory reporting by payment system operators (upravljavci plačilnih sistemov) on the operation of the systems they run — content, form and deadlines. This is the raw feed behind the annual payment/settlement systems report; the template itself shows which infrastructure metrics exist.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Nadzor nebančnih ponudnikov plačilnih storitev in infrastruktur finančnega trga
why_relevant: Oversight page for non-bank PSPs, e-money institutions and FMIs. Explains the legal mandate (TFEU, ESCB/ECB Statute, Zakon o Banki Slovenije, ZPlaSSIED) and links licensing decisions and oversight outputs — the regulatory layer around the card/POS acquiring market.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register subjektov nadzora (register of supervised entities)
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map for the SI payments market: banks and savings banks, EEA credit institutions and branches, payment system operators (upravljavci plačilnih sistemov), payment institutions, e-money institutions, AISPs, exempt payment institutions, currency exchangers, and SISBON/SISBIZ members. Names the competitor/partner universe that surrounds ATM/POS estates.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Primerjava stroškov bančnih storitev za potrošnike / prebivalstvo (bank fee comparison series)
why_relevant: Recurring (roughly semi-annual) bank-by-bank price comparison of a basket of payment services, including card issuance and maintenance fees, ATM withdrawal charges and account packages. Gives per-institution pricing that no aggregate statistic exposes — directly relevant to competitive analysis of card/ATM economics.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Mediji / Objave (press releases and statistical commentary)
why_relevant: The semi-annual payment-statistics narrative is issued here (e.g. releases stating 3.6 million cards outstanding, ~1,284-1,290 ATMs with 74% contactless, 47,000 POS terminals up 11% y/y, 330 million transactions worth EUR 186 billion in H1 2024), plus counterfeit-cash releases and payment-system reports. Fastest signal that new data has landed and the official interpretation of it.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Gotovina (cash section)
why_relevant: National cash authority pages: banknotes and coins in circulation, the euro changeover history, cash-handling rules and the counterfeiting sub-section. Core for the cash-usage topic and for contextualising declining ATM counts against cash demand.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Boj proti ponarejanju in statistika o ponaredkih (counterfeit statistics)
why_relevant: Annual national counterfeit-detection series (e.g. 1,181 counterfeit euro banknotes withdrawn in SI in 2024, ~7% more than 2023; EUR 20 and EUR 50 together >75% of counterfeits) with Eurosystem comparators. A cash-integrity indicator that pairs with cash-cycle and ATM/cash-handling demand.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Plačilna infrastruktura (payment infrastructure) and Poravnalni sistemi (settlement systems)
why_relevant: Describes the SI payment infrastructure landscape — TARGET services, SEPA IKP/instant payments, the domestic clearing arrangements and settlement systems — naming the operators (a route to Bankart and other processors) that sit behind card acquiring and ATM switching.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Plačilni instrumenti / Plačilne storitve in storitve izdajanja elektronskega denarja
why_relevant: Official definitions of payment instruments (payment cards, credit transfers, direct debits, e-money) and of licensed payment/e-money services under ZPlaSSIED. Supplies the authoritative Slovenian vocabulary used consistently across all BS statistical tables — the glossary anchor for this cell.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Nacionalni svet za plačila (National Payments Council)
why_relevant: BS-chaired multi-stakeholder forum on payments. Agendas, minutes and member lists reveal industry priorities, participating banks/processors/merchant bodies and forthcoming market changes months before they appear in statistics.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Digitalni evro (digital euro)
why_relevant: National-level communication on the digital euro project — the single largest medium-term structural risk/opportunity for card acceptance and ATM economics in SI. Forward-looking rather than statistical.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Metodološka pojasnila (methodological notes)
why_relevant: Cross-domain methodological reference (ESA2010 sectors, ECB balance-sheet methodology, revision policy and publication lags). Needed to interpret revisions and series breaks correctly, though its payment-statistics coverage is thinner than the dedicated reporting-instruction page.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – SDDS Plus nacionalna stran z zbirnimi podatki
why_relevant: IMF SDDS Plus national summary data page — a standardised, machine-friendly national data landing page with committed release timeliness. Useful as a stable cross-checking entry point and as evidence of publication commitments.

source_name: ECB Data Portal – Slovenia payment statistics (PSS/PTT) reference area SI
why_relevant: Banka Slovenije's payment-statistics returns under ECB/2013/43 are republished by the ECB in harmonised series (PSS/PTT keys with reference area SI). Provides an API-accessible, cross-country-comparable mirror of the same national data and a useful consistency check against the BS PxWeb tables. Adjacent to this cell but the direct downstream of it.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments and Settlement Systems Statistics (PSS) dataset
why_relevant: Master payments-statistics dataset of the ECB (ex-SDW). Slovenia (SI) appears as a country row for payment instruments, volumes/values, terminals, cards, and infrastructures under the harmonised ECB/2020/59 payments statistics regulation. This is the single most comparable machine-readable source for SI payment statistics.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — ATM, OTC and POS terminal transactions (PTT) dataset
why_relevant: The most granular EU-comparable series for ATM and POS terminal counts and transactions, with Slovenia available at annual and half-yearly frequency. Directly answers ATM/POS installed-base and throughput questions for the SI market.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Card payments and cash withdrawals using cards (PCP), incl. fraud data
why_relevant: Card transaction volumes/values and card-fraud series by country, including Slovenia; underpins card-penetration and card-fraud-rate benchmarking against euro area peers.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — SDMX 2.1 web service / bulk download documentation
why_relevant: Defines the machine access path (base URL https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service, CSV/SDMX-JSON/XML, dataflow discovery, bulk download). Essential engineering documentation for automating every ECB series in this cell.

source_name: ECB payments statistics press releases (semi-annual, e.g. first half of 2025)
why_relevant: Narrative + tables accompanying each semi-annual payments-statistics release; gives release calendar, revisions notes and headline euro-area context in which the SI row must be read.
